title: COP31: What will it take to deliver climate justice?
content: Fossil-fuel-driven industrialisation has pushed the world’s annual CO 2 emissions to nearly 40 billion tonnes per year and warmed the planet by about 1.3-1.4 o C above pre-industrial levels. Had all humanity lived like the American, warming would have reached at about 3.7°C. Following the average Luxembourger's lifestyle would have produced nearly 4°C of warming; living like the average Qatari would have pushed warming to a staggering 5°C or more. By contrast, scaling the historical Chinese lifestyle to all of humanity would have led to warming of only about 1.2°C — no higher than the Earth’s actual warming today. If everyone had lived like the average Indian, warming would have been lower still, at about 0.8°C. In 1928, Mahatma Gandhi wrote in Young India with remarkable prescience: “God forbid that India should ever take to industrialism after the manner of the West. If an entire nation of 300 million took to similar economic exploitation, it would strip the world bare like locusts.” A century later, Gandhi’s fears are being realised. Fossil-fuel-driven industrialisation has pushed the world’s annual CO 2 emissions to nearly 40 billion tonnes per year and warmed the planet by about 1.3-1.4 o C above pre-industrial levels. In September, the UN Environment Programme’s (UNEP’s) ‘Limiting Overshoot’ report warned that overshooting the 1.5 o C threshold is inevitable within the next three to four years.
